name: cafe
description:
The coffee shop as three independently-authored nets. The counter runs orders, the pantry holds stock, and staff are the people who can only do one thing at a time.

Starting a drink is one firing of all three: an event link fuses each start_X with the brew_X that pays for it and the acquire_X that takes a barista off the floor, so a drink is never begun without its ingredients being drawn down and someone actually making it. Finishing it is one firing of two — the drink is ready and the barista is free again.

That is what makes 'what if I put a third barista on?' answerable: headcount is `initial` on staff/available, and the queues it relieves live in a net that has never heard of staffing.

Fusing three nets fuses their arcs, and that is where the rate law has to be read carefully. After flattening, `start_X` consumes a pending order, a barista and a recipe's worth of stock, and `finish_X` consumes a busy barista. Only the pending order is a reason the shop goes faster; the barista and the beans are conditions on being allowed to start at all. They are marked `kinetic: false` in the subnets that own them, so they gate and are consumed without entering the firing rate — otherwise a bigger pantry brews quicker and two drinks in progress finish each other early. Demand sets the pace; everything else sets permission.
